title: Team Celebration Is the Glue That Binds People Together
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece elevates celebration above ordinary praise, describing it as praise 'with an exclamation point' that carries a distinct social and symbolic function beyond simple recognition. The author argues celebration's real power isn't the event itself but what it symbolizes, a public signal that binds team members together around shared accomplishment. The piece specifically pushes back on leaders who withhold celebration until final victory, and directly addresses and dismisses the fear that celebrating early progress will cause a team to coast.
points: Celebration is framed as categorically different from ordinary praise, a public, symbolic act that binds a team together.
The piece pushes back specifically on leaders who reserve celebration for final victory, recommending milestones along the way be marked too.
It directly names and dismisses a common leadership fear, that celebrating early creates complacency.
The closing claim is that celebrating more often actually generates more accomplishments worth celebrating.
quotes: Of the many forms of praise, including compliment, recognition, and approval, none is as energizing or motivational as celebration.
Celebration tells others to sit up and take notice of what has been achieved.

It is not the event or trappings of the celebration, nor the positive experience that creates its impact. Celebration is symbolic. It brings people together in a collaborative spirit of connectedness.
The fear that celebrated team members will slack off or presume success before the work is complete is unfounded.
The best leaders quickly learn that the more they celebrate, the more accomplishments there are to honor. Funny how that works.
